version.changelog: No user-facing changes in this version; documentation and function remain unchanged.

llm.summary: This is a disclosed Douyin analytics skill that uses a Redfox API key to look up account data, with some scoping and disclosure caveats but no evidence of hidden, destructive, or unrelated behavior.

dimensions.detail: The README, SKILL.md, workflow, and scripts consistently support the stated purpose: querying Douyin account/profile/work metadata from Redfox and generating a scored diagnostic report.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Natural-language triggers are broad, and the documentation has a Redfox-only data rule that conflicts with a web-search fallback for API failure; this is an output-integrity and accidental-invocation caveat, not evidence of malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install hooks, package-install behavior, obfuscation, startup registration, or automatic execution mechanism were found in the artifact files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires REDFOX_API_KEY and sends user-supplied Douyin account names or IDs to https://redfox.hk; this is proportionate to the purpose and mostly disclosed through API configuration and data-flow docs, though a clearer privacy notice would improve informed consent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No privilege escalation, credential harvesting, background worker, broad local indexing, or persistent agent behavior was found; one example script writes a local markdown report only when run directly.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable configuring a Redfox API key and having the Douyin account names or IDs you enter sent to Redfox for lookup, potentially consuming API credits. Prefer explicit commands and treat any non-Redfox fallback result as lower confidence.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: The documented fallback to web search conflicts with the strict Redfox-only data-source rule. This should be cleaned up because it can weaken report provenance, but the code inspected does not implement hidden web retrieval or data exfiltration.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger examples are consistent with a natural-language assistant skill, but because each lookup can call a paid third-party API, users should invoke it explicitly and agents should confirm ambiguous requests.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending Douyin account identifiers to Redfox is central to the skill and is reflected in the API endpoint, key, cost, and data-flow documentation. The concern is under-disclosure rather than unexpected data handling.
